tasks.source_level_statement: For a finite set S of complex nodes excluding r and conjugate r, Im r != 0, construct a polynomial P with P(r)=i, P(conjugate r)=-i, P(w)=0 for w in S, and P(conjugate z)=conjugate(P(z)). S need not be conjugation-closed.
The two selected squared values with arbitrary positive weights m1,m2 contribute -(m1+m2). No equality of multiplicities or fourfold orbit weights is assumed.
G_L(z)=P(z)*exp(-L*((z-Re r)^2+(Im r)^2)); norm squared is |P(z)|^2 exp(-2 L D(z)), D=(Re z-Re r)^2+(Im r)^2-(Im z)^2. G_L agrees with P at r and conjugate r.
For |Im z|<=1/2 and |Re z-Re r|>=1, D>=3/4 and |G_(n+1)(z)|^2 <= exp(-3n/2)*|G_1(z)|^2 for all natural n. P and finite S are fixed before n.
If b is summable and ||f_i||<=q*b_i, prove f summable and ||sum f_i||<=q*sum b_i. From any mass>0 and finite C obtain n with exp(-3n/2)*C<mass, not by an unproved terminating search.
